document_notes: Section 1 note: Several of these papers (e.g., #57, #78, #92, #89/#94, #136) report cardiovascular and respiratory hospital admissions as broad, pre-specified diagnostic categories (often built from CMS/Medicare claims) rather than single ICD codes — the ranges above reflect the standard groupings used in that literature (e.g., NMMAPS/Medicare cardiovascular and respiratory admission definitions).

ICD-9-CM vs. ICD-10-CM: U.S. claims data (Medicare/Medicaid) transitioned from ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM on October 1, 2015. Papers using data before this date use ICD-9; papers using more recent data use ICD-10 or a crosswalk.

"Cardiovascular" and "respiratory" admissions in air pollution epidemiology are frequently defined using standardized code groupings from the NMMAPS/Medicare literature (often built off the AHRQ Clinical Classifications Software or the ICD-9 ranges 390–459 and 460–519, respectively) rather than single diagnosis codes — this is the convention in most of Dr. Dominici's cardiorespiratory papers.

Where a paper's exact ICD code list was not published in the abstract/title, the codes shown reflect standard definitions used in equivalent published methods (e.g., Medicare claims-based hospitalization studies).
